our_interpretation: The plain reading concerns demonstrated capabilities available in 2022, not proof that every possible future convolutional architecture must fail.
Solving broadly means reliable performance across major kinds of AI work, including unfamiliar reasoning problems.
I use the current-year reporting window ending on the post date for this ongoing technical claim. There is no standard quarterly reporting period for AI capabilities.
The attribution to LeCun requires the original tweets and their context; evidence of technical limitations alone cannot verify that attribution.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporary evidence establishes substantial unsolved capabilities across major AI tasks, and the original tweets substantiate the broad claim attributed to LeCun.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Contemporary evaluations establish reliable broad capability, or the original tweets clearly make a materially narrower claim than Marcus attributes to LeCun.

evidence.explanation: The evaluation documents an important remaining limitation in learning visual reasoning tasks. It also finds convolutional architectures stronger than transformers on most tested measures, so it supports a limited capability critique rather than a blanket dismissal.

Meta's account acknowledges limitations in contemporary AI and describes reasoning and planning as research challenges. It concerns AI broadly and does not establish what LeCun said in the October tweets.

The authors report strong results on particular visual reasoning problems. This qualifies any suggestion that convolutional networks cannot reason at all, but does not establish broad general competence.
